key_insight: Ligand-exchanged AgBiS2 nanocrystals enable thicker near-infrared absorbers for tandem photovoltaics, with 24.0% efficiency demonstrated in four-terminal perovskite tandems.
engineering_relevance: One-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 films offers a route toward stable, scalable near-infrared sub-cells with improved charge extraction at greater thickness.
method: Model tandem optical performance using the experimental AgBiS2 absorption spectrum.
Develop solution-phase ligand exchange to enable roughly tenfold thicker films with efficient carrier extraction.
Integrate AgBiS2 with visible-absorbing perovskites in four-terminal and monolithic tandems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports modeled triple-junction efficiencies above 47.5%, measured four-terminal tandem efficiency of 24.0%, monolithic voltage addition, and over 90% efficiency retention after three months of unencapsulated dry-air storage.
watch_item: The modeled efficiency potential remains unproven experimentally, and dry-air storage stability does not establish durability under operating conditions.
paper_title: AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
